## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Ekarājacariya* ("The Conduct of the One King") is a text in the *Cariyāpiṭaka* collection of the Pali canon [SuttaCentral]. In this narrative, the Bodhisatta is depicted in a past life as the renowned monarch Ekarājā, who firmly undertakes and resolutely determines upon supreme morality (*paramaṁ sīlaṁ adhiṭṭhāya*) [Lim 2009]. Valuing omniscience above all else, he establishes his firm resolve, proclaiming in the concluding verses that no one equalled him in resolute determination (*adhiṭṭhānapāramī*) [Lim 2009].
In scholarly discussion of early Buddhist doctrine, the text serves as a key exemplar of the perfection of resolute determination (*adhiṭṭhāna*) and moral resolve [Lim 2009].
Regarding text reuse and parallels, DharmaNexus detects 17 matching segments (940 characters) between the *Ekarājacariya* and its commentary, the *Cariyāpiṭaka-aṭṭhakathā*, with the most extensive match occurring at segments §3.2–4.4 [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also records low-scoring automatic text alignments with a Tibetan commentary, the *Bhagavatsarvadurgatipariṣodhanatejorajatathāgatārhatsamyaksaṃbuddhamahātantrarājavyākhyāsundarālaṃkāra* (D2626), though no curated external parallels are established by SuttaCentral [DharmaNexus; SuttaCentral].
